fullPassage: Whenever a business wants to grow, it has to find investors, who are people that are willing to give the business the money that it needs. In return, the investors get a part of the business' profits (if there are any). Somewhere along the way, someone got the bright idea to divide up a company into "shares" or "stocks". Each share would represent a certain percentage of the profits. If the company did well and made a lot of profits, the shares would become worth lots of money, because they would pay the investors lots of money each year. Men (called "brokers") would gather in downtown New York City and sell these shares to interested investors. Eventually, the brokers for these large companies moved their business into a building, and the New York Stock Exchange on Wall Street was born.

det.korean: ② willingly → willing: be willing to 구문에서 be동사 뒤에 형용사 willing이 와야 함. willingly는 부사.
det.analysis:
✅ ① who: 선행사 investors(사람)를 수식하는 관계대명사 who — 적절
❌ ② willingly: be + 형용사 + to 구문 → willing(형용사)이 정답. willingly(부사)는 be동사 보어 불가 ←정답
✅ ③ would: 과거 습관/추측의 조동사 would — 적절
✅ ④ interested: 감정형용사 interested + 명사 investors — 적절
det.tip: be willing to(기꺼이 ~하다): be + 형용사 + to부정사. 부사(willingly)가 아닌 형용사(willing) 필요.
